# Preface {.unnumbered}

Here's a short exercise in linguistics using a document that has been translated into thousands of languages. This site presents the text of the Lord's Prayer from the Gospels of Matthew and Luke in several languages. It also includes transliterations for the Greek versions and playable audio.


## Listening

Most chapters have a **Listen** button that reads the prayer aloud and highlights each line as it is said. Where the browser reports word boundaries, the button reads each word individually.

Most chapters use the voice that your device has for that language. This is why the reading follows the text exactly; each line is spoken as its own utterance, so there is nothing to synchronize. If your device has no voice for a language, the button will say so instead of appearing and failing.

Latin is the other exception. Since no browser ships with a Latin voice, that chapter plays a real recording from Wikimedia Commons instead: a spoken reading. However, a recording carries no idea of where one line ends and the next begins, so it plays without following the text line by line.


## The eight chapters

| Chapter | Text |
|---|---|
| [Ancient Greek](chapters/ancient-greek.qmd) | The Koine original, NA28 and Patriarchal 1904 |
| [Modern Greek](chapters/modern-greek.qmd) | The demotic rendering |
| [Latin](chapters/latin.qmd) | Roman Missal and Vulgata Clementina |
| [Lithuanian](chapters/lithuanian.qmd) | Catholic and Orthodox forms |
| [Spanish](chapters/spanish.qmd) | Scío / Reina-Valera, with the liturgical variant |
| [Italian](chapters/italian.qmd) | The 2020 Missal and the Waldensian text |
| [German](chapters/german.qmd) | Ecumenical 1968, Luther, Einheitsübersetzung |
| [English](chapters/english.qmd) | BCP 1662, traditional ecumenical, ELLC 1988 |

Full provenance for every text is in [Sources](chapters/sources.qmd).
